information.content: Topical macrocyclic lactone used for fleas, mites and selected nematode/heartworm indications in mammals, plus selected avian and amphibian parasite protocols.
Highly toxic to aquatic organisms. Do not use in chelonians because neurotoxicity/death is a concern.
Anti-ascaridial anthelmintic used for adult ascarids and non-encysted GI nematodes. It has no larvicidal activity, so repeat dosing is usually required.
Do not use with pyrantel because the mechanisms are antagonistic. Monitor for tremors or ataxia.
Imidazothiazole anthelmintic used for nematodes in selected mammals, reptiles, amphibians and fish. It is particularly useful for some hedgehog lungworm/nematode cases.
Avoid debilitated animals and birds. The therapeutic index is low in birds and severe toxicity has been reported.
Insect growth regulator that prevents flea egg development and has specialist aquatic use against crustacean ectoparasites.
It does not kill adult fleas, so an appropriate adulticide/environmental plan is required for active flea infestations.
Phenylpyrazole ectoparasiticide used topically in selected bird and reptile mite/ectoparasite situations.
Avoid amphibians and fish. Many fipronil products are dangerous to aquatic organisms and birds if misused.
Topical parasiticide combinations used in selected small mammals and reptiles for ectoparasites and some internal parasites.
Many combinations include ingredients that are hazardous to birds or aquatic organisms. Check exact product composition before use.
Benzimidazole anthelmintic used primarily as an immersion treatment for fish flukes and internal nematodes.
Low solubility and high potency make product selection and water dosing accuracy important.
Broad-spectrum amphenicol antimicrobial used for bacterial disease in fish by injection or in-feed protocols.
Use responsible antibiotic principles and culture/sensitivity where possible.
Formalin bath treatment used in aquatic species for protozoan and some monogenean ectoparasites.
Handle with PPE. It removes dissolved oxygen, irritates gills and should not be used above 27°C.
Immersion/topical dye used for water mould/fungal infections and some protozoal ectoparasites in fish.
Teratogenic/suspected carcinogen, stains materials and can cause irreversible respiratory toxicity if overdosed or used in sensitive fish.
Oxidising water treatment used for external bacteria and ectoparasites in freshwater fish; also used topically for avian nail/talon cautery.
Do not use with formalin and do not use in sea water. Some species and aquarium systems are sensitive.
Peripheral opioid agonist used short-term for selected diarrhoea or severe GI motility cases in mammals.
Contraindicated with intestinal obstruction. In rabbits, use only briefly because worsening GI stasis is a concern.

pearls.pearl: Selamectin is a skin-drop drug with aquarium consequences. Keep the fish tank out of the blast radius.
Piperazine only tackles adult ascarids. It is a mop, not a time machine for larvae.
Levamisole and birds are a narrow-ledge situation. Pick a different path unless specialist guidance says otherwise.
Lufenuron stops flea nurseries, not adult flea parties. Pair it with adult control when there are live fleas.
With fipronil, species choice is the safety catch. Reptile wipe, not amphibian soup.
Combination spot-ons are ingredient jungles. Read the product, not just the brand name.
Fish bath medicines are water chemistry medicines wearing drug costumes.
If fish are not eating, in-feed antibiotics are theatre with no audience.
Formalin steals oxygen while fighting parasites. Aeration is part of the prescription.
Malachite green is effective dye-dragon medicine, but it burns the wrong fish if you invite it carelessly.
The pink colour is not decoration. It is the active permanganate telling you it still exists.
Loperamide can quiet diarrhoea, but in rabbits it can also quiet the bowel. Use briefly and suspiciously.
